operations.name: Antonio Caseres

expected.name: Antonio Caseres
expected.description: Antonio Caseres was prosecuted under United States wartime statutes of the World War I era (chiefly the Espionage Act, the Sedition Act, or the Selective Service Act). Recorded offense: Conspiracy. Sentence: 1 year and 1 day. Sentenced February 5, 1920. Held at the Leavenworth Federal Penitentiary. Later disposition: Paroled from Leavenworth; Parole violated Sept. 25. This case is documented in the 1921 U.S. Senate hearing "Amnesty and Pardon for Political Prisoners" (digitized by the Internet Archive).
expected.body:
1920s release-date review: Released on parole August 9, 1920. The report separately records a parole violation September 25 and sentence expiration November 25, 1920; neither establishes a later physical release. Any return to custody remains undocumented.

Source: Amnesty and Pardon for Political Prisoners (1921), printed page 194, Attorney General's January 20, 1921 report, list of persons paroled. The original table was visually checked; sentence expiration and parole approval are distinguished from release.

operations.source: National Archives Leavenworth inmate index lists Antonio Caseres, register14920: https://www.archives.gov/kansas-city/finding-aids/leavenworth-penitentiary/inmates-c.html . Existing portrait, sentencing date and parole endpoint preserved. No admission date inferred from sentence.

operations.name: Katherine Lincoln

expected.name: Katherine Lincoln
expected.description: Katherine Lincoln was a member of the National Woman's Party and one of the "Silent Sentinels" imprisoned during the 1917-1919 campaign to picket the Wilson White House for woman suffrage. Held at the Occoquan Workhouse in Virginia or the District of Columbia Jail, many of these prisoners joined hunger strikes and were force-fed.
